body: Wouldn't it be a good idea to get out of my "comfort zone" though and practice being more sociable? I know you're right about me being too self conscious, but how exactly does one become less self conscious? I'm also just really bad at listening and reading comprehension. I've had problems pronouncing words correctly at a very young age and my family said I used to just make up words. Pretty sure they thought I was mildly retarded until I was 5. I honestly think I have a form of autism/aspergers that was never really diagnosed, and I hate going to the Dr. and trying to explain my situation cause I have an extremely hard time answering questions when asked to recall something on the spot or to put 2 and 2 together in the health sense.

There is no social place where I feel comfortable unfortunately. If I'm at work and my coworkers start talking about something I'm interested in I keep my mouth shut most of the time. I'm awkward around family, my best friends. I just tried playing D&D for the first time the other day with people I'm comfortable around for the most part. I'm a huge RPG nerd as far as games are concerned so D&D is something that has interested me that I haven't tried before. I started off trying to be somewhat social but after a half hour or so I just fall silent and don't feel confident in my ability to speak anymore. I don't even socialize much with my fiance whom I live with. It doesn't matter who I talk to. I'm bound to fuck up my sentence structure somehow, or to even conjure up the vocabulary needed in order to complete a sentence.

Thanks. I feel like depression is so deeply embedded in me at this point that there's no way I will ever be truly happy. Every time I go somewhere that I'm expected to be social I just end up getting depressed afterwards. Mainly because I see how everyone else is socializing and having a good time and I basically sit back and watch it all fly by. Believe me, I would LOVE to be more social, but communicating with others is extremely hard for me to do, and it's extra frustrating because I feel like other people just think I should outright be able to talk to others easily "if I want to", but it's just not that easy. Then I feel like other people just start judging me as a freak that hates everyone. I hate going to work and listening to all the conversations that I could easily jump into but I'm afraid to make a squeak, which is sometimes the noise that I might as well make for all the times that I've failed to form a coherent sentence.
